summary: Frontend-only regression testing of the NavLink active-state bug fix in Therapist and Client portals. All 12 nav items across both portals now activate their SOLE entry when clicked, both dashboards no longer stay 'stuck' active on sub-routes, and direct-URL navigation correctly highlights the target nav. Perceived latency issue was cosmetic (stuck highlight) — target pages now render in well under 2 seconds (measured 0.02s–0.16s each).
critical_code_review_comments: TherapistPortal.jsx and ClientPortal.jsx are 552 and 491 lines — approaching the >700-line split threshold but currently acceptable. If more feature modules are added, consider splitting sub-routes (Clients, Calendar, Requests, etc.) into their own files under /pages/therapist/ and /pages/client/.

Both portals duplicate the Shell + NAV pattern (identical NavLink block, mobile bar, logout footer). Extract into a shared <PortalShell nav={...} /> component to remove ~40 lines of duplication per file and prevent this class of bug (relative vs absolute `to`) from re-occurring in future portals.

NavLink `end={!!end}` requires every future NAV entry to remember to set `end: true` on the index route. A safer, self-explanatory alternative is a custom NavItem using `useLocation()` with explicit `location.pathname === to` for index, `startsWith(to + '/')` for parents — this was flagged as an acceptable alternative in the request and would eliminate the footgun.

Nested `<Routes>` inside a portal Shell means every NavLink relative `to` was silently matched against ancestors; the fix to absolute paths is correct but the mobile bar (~line 73 in TherapistPortal, ~line 69 in ClientPortal) must be kept in sync manually — worth a comment or a shared constant (already done via NAV, good).
context_for_next_testing_agent: NavLink active-state fix verified across both portals (Therapist: Dashboard/Clients/Calendar/Requests/Resources/Profile — Client: Dashboard/Appointments/Journal/Homework/Resources/Profile). Absolute paths + `end: true` on Dashboard NAV entry is working. Page loads observed 0.02s–0.16s — no latency issue. Two 401 console errors observed on the /login page (likely GET /api/auth/me before login) — expected behavior, unauth calls.

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: In both portal shells, the sidebar NavLink used relative `to=''` inside a nested <Routes>. Without `end`, React Router's NavLink matched any descendant route, so the 'Dashboard' entry stayed active on every sub-route. Users saw the dashboard nav item never de-highlight and interpreted it as 'nothing happened' when clicking Calendar/Resources/Requests/Profile — even though the sub-routes actually loaded (in ~50–150ms).
rca_of_the_issue.fix_applied_by_main_agent: NAV constant now uses ABSOLUTE paths (/therapist, /therapist/calendar, ... and /portal, /portal/appointments, ...). Each entry passes an optional `end: true` flag which is threaded into <NavLink end={!!end}>. This is set only on the Dashboard/index entry, so only the exact-match Dashboard route requires strict matching; sibling routes match by their full absolute path.
rca_of_the_issue.verification: All 12 nav entries (6 per portal) verified to become the SOLE active entry when navigated to via click AND via direct URL. Content headings render within <200ms per route — well inside the 2-second SLA.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation_for_future: Adopt a custom NavItem with useLocation() (main agent noted this as acceptable alternative) OR extract shared <PortalShell> to prevent duplication and this pattern from recurring in future portals.
